language.description: A semantic programming and transport language in which stable meaning is identified independently from source spelling, file location, representation, and browser rendering.
language.identity_rule: Semantic identity is stable; representations may vary.
language.source_of_truth_rule: Until the semantic compiler/runtime is declared authoritative, executable repository source remains runtime truth and the canonical language contract governs interpretation, generation, translation, and validation.

semantic_identities.CHID: Code Handle ID. Persistent semantic identity for a code symbol independent of name, path, line, language, or UI representation.
semantic_identities.GLYPH: Contextual or compound meaning composed from Runes and/or other Glyphs.
semantic_identities.SHAEP: Spatial Hot Preservation Object. Current authoritative format is SHAEP v2: persistent ShaepId, preserved native source/provenance, and a canonical hot archive representation.
semantic_identities.CCTV: Trusted context translation/verification boundary under development. It resolves authenticated/effective identity, protected resource context, Recursive Authority path, and intent into contextual capability. Its long-form expansion is not yet canon.

epistemic_domains.FACT: Asserted true inside the declared real/system scope with evidence or provenance.
epistemic_domains.HYPOTHESIS: A possibility being explored. It must not silently mutate FACT.
epistemic_domains.FICTION: Deliberately invented or world-canon material. It may be true inside a fictional scope without becoming a real-world FACT.
epistemic_domains.UNKNOWN: Unresolved or insufficiently supported. UNKNOWN is not false and is not random chance.

boolean_semantics.epistemic_unknown: UNKNOWN is available where the active schema/domain permits epistemic uncertainty.
boolean_semantics.rule: Numeric 0, 1, and -1 have no universal boolean meaning in the semantic layer. A target or wire representation may map numbers to booleans only when that mapping is explicitly declared by its schema.

humans_surface.name: Humans
humans_surface.role: Human-readable epistemic/control-flow surface for the same semantic system.

keywords.Then: Execute the consequent behavior when the active condition holds.
keywords.Maybe: Mark a value, branch, or statement UNKNOWN/uncertain rather than random.
keywords.Maybeif: Conditional exploration whose premise remains uncertain.
keywords.Else: Fallback branch when the preceding condition does not hold.
keywords.Dont: Negate/prohibit the following action or condition according to its declared scope.
keywords.Because: Attach provenance, evidence, or rationale. Because does not itself prove causation.

representation_rules: ASCII characters, source-language keywords, numeric opcodes, JSON names, binary encodings, pixels, and UI controls are representations of semantic identities; they are not the identities themselves.
Values are operands/results and are not generally equal to the operations that consume or produce them.
Textually duplicated code is not automatically semantically duplicated code.
A semantic relation must declare its relation type and any conditions under which equivalence holds.

instruction_model.canonical_shape: semantic identity/opcode + typed operands + explicit target/scope when required
instruction_model.compact_example_note: Compact character streams are illustrative until a versioned, unambiguous token grammar defines operand types, lengths, blocks, negative/float/string values, symbols, and boundaries.

cctv_contract.input: authenticated identity + effective/delegated identity when applicable + protected resource/SHAEP + active authority path + intent + trusted context
cctv_contract.output: contextual capability Glyph and/or allowlisted Rune stream
cctv_contract.rule: Expose capability without exposing the credential that created it. Resolve Recursive Authority on the trusted side and deny ambiguous permission paths rather than guessing.

perception_request_model.meaning: Human 52, Character 1, X=23, Y=42, Z=74, Tier=1, Layer=9, Intent=Inspect.
perception_request_model.hidden_state_rule: Hidden traps, reveal thresholds/DCs, GM notes, unrevealed objects, and other protected facts remain on the trusted side until reveal is authorized.

pixel_property_model.rule: A pixel or screen coordinate locates a current representation; it is not persistent semantic identity.
pixel_property_model.resolution: pixel/screen position -> current representation node/hit target -> CHID or semantic UI identity -> permitted Rune/Glyph action
pixel_property_model.accessibility: Pointer, touch, keyboard, voice, switch input, and screen-reader actions may resolve to the same semantic action without sharing the same pixel.

decoder_contract.dispatch_rule: Use pre-registered, versioned handlers for known Rune/Glyph opcodes. Reject unknown instructions before execution.
decoder_contract.state_rule: Resolve semantic targets through CHID/SHAEP identity and update only affected representations/dependencies when possible.

security.principle: The language may be public; authority determines what it is allowed to do.
requirements: Never treat compact or binary encoding as authorization.
Never evaluate arbitrary incoming source strings.
Use authenticated actor identity and scoped Recursive Authority/capabilities.
Version semantic definitions and never silently change an opcode's meaning.
Reject malformed, unknown, out-of-scope, over-budget, or unauthorized instructions.
Audit actor -> instruction -> target -> authority decision -> state revision -> affected CHIDs/SHAEPs.
Use anti-replay/sequence or revision controls where repeated commands would be unsafe.
Do not send hidden authoritative state to a client before that context is allowed to perceive it.

provenance.rule: Provenance persists through copying and modification. Unknown provenance defaults to the outsider/red boundary rather than silently becoming HUMAN.

error_law.rule: Normalized recurring failures are linked to code IDs/CHIDs and, where known, Rune/Glyph semantics. A previously resolved failure that reappears is a regression, distinct from an ordinary repeat.

agent_bootstrap: Read .code-index/humans_language.json and docs/SHAELVIEN_SEMANTIC_LANGUAGE.md before generating, translating, refactoring, or decoding Shaelvien semantic code.
Use this deployed manifest for discovery and compatibility metadata, then load the canonical sources listed under discovery when the task touches their domain.
Search existing CHIDs and semantic units before creating a new concept; reuse identity when the concept is the same.
Do not infer semantic identity from spelling, filename, line number, ASCII token, numeric opcode, pixel, or target-language syntax.
Do not infer numeric truthiness; use typed boolean semantics or an explicitly declared encoding map.
Keep FACT, HYPOTHESIS, FICTION, and UNKNOWN distinct and explicit.
Treat compact-token and perception-packet examples as non-canonical unless a later contract version marks their grammar canonical.
Preserve provenance and authority boundaries in generated code and translations.
Treat CCTV as a trusted verification/translation boundary and do not invent its long-form expansion.

When repository behavior and this experimental language layer disagree, do not silently rewrite working behavior; report the mismatch and preserve executable truth while the semantic layer is reconciled.

compatibility.target_rule: Target-language syntax is a generated or observed representation of semantic meaning, not the semantic identity itself.
